tau_proxy_warning: Every tau figure in this file is a PROXY, not a measured accepted length. The offline evaluator multiplies MARGINAL per-position agreement rates against corpus tokens; that product is not the joint probability of an accepted prefix. Its numerical closeness to a served accepted length does not validate it. Fix the evaluator to compute the joint accepted-prefix probability before quoting tau again.

training_curve.held_out: 496 rows (corpus rows 99,457-99,956), cached identically, never trained on
training_curve.definition: tau_proxy = 1 + sum_k prod_{j<=k} p_j, where p_j are MARGINAL per-position agreement rates
training_curve.note: Training stopped after epoch 7 of a planned 10: the last epoch delta was +0.026 proxy tau, epochs 8-10 were projected at about +0.01 for roughly $65, and a mid-run host slowdown pushed the 10-epoch cost past the ceiling. Two differently-trained proxy points cannot establish a data-scaling law; an earlier claim that more data was exhausted has been withdrawn as unsupported.
training_curve.label: measured (the agreement numbers) / proxy (what tau means)

served_accepted_length.note: This IS a measured accepted length, from the engine's own acceptance counters, and it is the number to cite rather than the proxy.
served_accepted_length.label: measured, preliminary (single boot, 2026-09-08)

teacher_forced_agreement.criterion: replay each arm's emitted continuation as prompt_logprobs=2 over (prompt + emitted); an emitted token passes when it equals the target's argmax at that position. 25,600 tokens per arm.
teacher_forced_agreement.reference_control: the AR arm scores 0.975586 against a spec-off server and 0.973203 against a spec-on server, so the reference itself moves 0.24 pp between boots and differences below about 0.3 pp are engine noise
not_a_certification: The check covers ALL emitted tokens, including correction and bonus tokens — not only accepted drafts.
Replay used different prefixes across arms, and prefill versus decode execution differs.
Recorded maximum mismatch margins exceed 12 log units, so the earlier claim that 'all mismatches are near-ties' is false (the MEDIAN margin at mismatches is 0.25; the maximum is not).
The AR control itself mismatches at about 2.4%, so an accept-path bug touching under ~2% of emitted tokens is invisible to this check.

What is missing for a real certification: common-prefix controls, rejection/rollback coverage, mismatch rate broken out by position-within-block (a real bug concentrates at one offset, noise does not), and a pre-declared non-inferiority margin.
teacher_forced_agreement.label: measured, preliminary (single boot, 2026-09-08). Losslessness is NOT certified.

engine_nondeterminism.reading: The engine agrees with itself at 20.4% on a bit-identical rerun at c=1, temperature 0. Both comparisons diverge at the same median position (20.0 / 20.5) and share the same 9 requests diverging at position 0. The implied per-token argmax flip rate is about 2.7%, which caps the resolution of every fidelity check on this stack — including the teacher-forced one above. It was accepted as a noise floor and never investigated.
engine_nondeterminism.label: measured, preliminary
